definitions.explanation: The ability to read and write, or the act of reading and writing. Often used to refer to basic literacy skills.

examples.japanese: {読|よ}み{書|か}き⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{読|よ}み{書|か}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{教|おし}える→教える：00526_oshieru⟧。
examples.english: I teach children reading and writing.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{読|よ}み{書|か}き⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{漢字|かんじ}→漢字：09480_kanji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で⟦{時間|じかん}がかかる→時間がかかる：26082_jikangakakaru⟧。
examples.english: Japanese reading and writing takes time because there are so many kanji.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧ (to read) and ⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧ (to write), referring to the fundamental literacy skills. Often used in educational contexts and discussions about language ability.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {読|よ}み{書|か}き⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧: to be able to read and write
- {読|よ}み{書|か}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{習|なら}う→習う：00479_narau⟧: to learn reading and writing
- {読|よ}み{書|か}きそろばん: reading, writing, and arithmetic (the three Rs)

RELATED WORDS:
- {識字|しきじ}: literacy — more formal and used in academic or policy contexts
- {文盲|もんもう}: illiteracy — inability to read and write
